paper.title_en: Observation of a sub-Hertz-level Bloch-Siegert shift in a Floquet-engineered optical lattice clock
paper.abstract_en: When a two-level quantum system is driven periodically with a Rabi frequency <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> comparable to the driving frequency <math><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></math>, the resonant transition frequency deviates from the bare energy gap—an effect known as the Bloch-Siegert shift. Observing sub-Hertz Bloch-Siegert shift is challenging due to its small energy scale and its mixing with other systematic shifts. Using a Floquet-engineered optical lattice clock, we directly observe this sub-hertz shift in ultracold atoms. We tune driving parameters to suppress micromotion and apply a self-comparison stroboscopic method to remove unwanted frequency shifts. Assisted by closed-loop feedback, we achieve high-precision results after one hour of averaging and longer integration will further improve the measurement accuracy.
